item.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption reviews systemic weaknesses in public procurement and proposes reforms for government.
item.support: The work of the ICAC indicates that statewide corruption risks with regard to procurement stem from a combination of system design and implementation weaknesses
item.section: NSW government procurement: the Commission’s interest

item.text: Its research includes surveys of agencies and suppliers, interviews, focus groups, policy analysis and review of investigation and complaint data.
item.support: conducted interviews and focus groups with public sector procurement specialists and suppliers to government
item.section: NSW government procurement: the Commission’s interest

item.text: The Commission concludes that unclear leadership, fragmented structures and complex rules weaken procurement, alongside inadequate support and compliance oversight.
item.support: The ICAC’s examination of NSW public sector procurement has revealed a system that has grown and evolved over time without any clear leadership

item.text: Its seven recommendations cover central leadership, a system review, simpler and aligned rules, better advice, staff competence and compliance monitoring.
item.support: This report makes the following seven recommendations aimed at establishing clear leadership
item.section: NSW government procurement: the Commission’s interest

item.quote: The central agencies have focused on their policy considerations at the expense of providing assistance through effective information, advice, and support.
